scope: Pillars security, reliability, performance, costOptimization; operational excellence and sustainability not reviewed (by request)
evidenceBase: https://github.com/sriram-um/aws-containerized-microservices (main @ 8aae8bd: the architecture as built, before decommissioning) + read-only checks of account 977534234172 on 2026-11-01

COST1.title: How do you design your container build process to avoid unnecessary cost?
COST1.notes:
Evidence: ECR lifecycle policies (keep 10 images, expire untagged after 1 day); multi-stage builds; native ARM CodeBuild (21 s vs 365 s emulated) with local Docker layer cache; requirements.txt holds production dependencies only (dev dependencies separate).
Gap: No shared internal base image for common dependencies (each service installs its own).

COST2.title: Ensure that your container images contain only what is relevant for your application to run
COST2.notes:
Evidence: Start-up measured (Fargate created->running 32-35 s); no volumes, read-only root filesystem, only the venv and the app code in the image (54-75 MB).
Gap: None significant.

COST3.title: How do you reduce your container images size?
COST3.notes:
Evidence: Multi-stage Dockerfile: the runtime stage adds 3 layers to the base (user, venv, code); a naive single-stage build added 33 MB vs 11 MB (Phase 1).
Gap: None significant.

COST4.title: How do you design your containerized application to support automatic scaling and graceful termination?
COST4.notes:
Evidence: Exec-form CMD, so uvicorn is PID 1 and receives SIGTERM; graceful stop measured (1.9 s locally, 0.1 s in ECS after ALB draining; Spot simulation 453/453 ok); target tracking scaling.
Gap: None significant.

COST5.title: How do you design your containerized application to support multiple CPU architectures?
COST5.notes:
Evidence: Deliberately built for arm64/Graviton (buildx --platform linux/arm64, ARM CodeBuild, RuntimePlatform ARM64) after comparing price/performance; local amd64 builds for development.
Gap: Images are single-architecture (no multi-arch manifest), so an x86 fallback would need a rebuild.

COST6.title: How do you minimize cost for your containerized application during startup time?
COST6.notes:
Evidence: Connection pool opened without waiting for the DB, JWKS fetched lazily and cached, slim image; Fargate image pull 3.7-4.6 s for 57 MB.
Gap: Image lazy loading (SOCI) not evaluated.

COST7.title: What systems are you using to create your container build process?
COST7.notes:
Evidence: CodePipeline V2 + CodeBuild (ARM) per service, path-filtered triggers, immutable SHA tags.
Gap: None significant.

PERF1.title: How do you reduce the size of your container image?
PERF1.notes:
Evidence: python:3.12-slim base; one process per container (uvicorn; the ADOT collector is a separate sidecar); allow-list .dockerignore (only requirements.txt and the package).
Gap: Distroless/minimal bases not evaluated.

PERF2.title: How do you reduce the pull time of your container image?
PERF2.notes:
Evidence: ECR in the same Region via VPC endpoints; the collector image via an ECR pull-through cache instead of public.ecr.aws.
Gap: None significant.

PERF3.title: How do you make sure to get consistent results for your target images?
PERF3.notes:
Evidence: Images tagged with the git SHA in IMMUTABLE repositories; base image pinned to 3.12.16-slim-trixie (digest checked identical across registries); dependency versions pinned.
Gap: The base image is pinned by tag, not by digest.

PERF4.title: How do you make sure to use updated versions for parent images?
PERF4.notes:
Evidence: Base image version pinned and documented; HIGH CVEs re-checked manually.
Gap: No notification or automation when the parent image or its packages are updated (no EventBridge/Inspector/Dependabot trigger).

PERF5.title: How do you make sure you get consistent performance results over time?
PERF5.notes:
Evidence: Load tests (scripts/load_test.py) with results kept as CSV in docs/.
Gap: Performance tests are manual and not part of the pipeline; no regression thresholds.

PERF6.title: How do you optimize the size of your target image?
PERF6.notes:
Evidence: CodeBuild LOCAL_DOCKER_LAYER_CACHE + LOCAL_SOURCE_CACHE; ARM64 Graviton selected for price/performance (Fargate ARM $0.03238/vCPU-h vs x86 $0.04048).
Gap: None significant.

REL1.title: How do you limit the amount of CPU and memory a container consumes?
REL1.notes:
Evidence: Task-level 256 CPU units / 512 MiB; collector sidecar limited to 64 CPU units / 128 MiB hard, 64 MiB soft.
Gap: None significant.

REL2.title: How do you handle persistent data in a container application?
REL2.notes:
Evidence: Containers are stateless; all persistent data lives in Aurora and DynamoDB, and the root filesystem is read-only.
Gap: None.

REL3.title: How do you automate building and testing of containers?
REL3.notes:
Evidence: Local: docker compose with Postgres plus an optional local ADOT collector for span checks; pytest (moto, local JWKS keys); CI runs the same tests before every image build.
Gap: No dedicated test/staging environment in the pipeline (tests run in CodeBuild, then straight to production with a canary).

REL4.title: How do I cascade updates to a parent or base image?
REL4.notes:
Evidence: Both services use the same pinned parent image (ECR Public mirror of python:3.12.16-slim-trixie); Dockerfiles and all images are under source control, images tagged with the commit SHA.
Gap: No image hierarchy (no organization base image built once and inherited) and no automatic rebuild when the parent changes.

REL5.title: How do you monitor the health of a container?
REL5.notes:
Evidence: Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK; task definition health checks (app /health without DB dependency, collector /healthcheck); ALB target health on /health; unhealthy tasks are replaced by ECS.
Gap: None significant.

SEC1.title: How do you ensure that your container images are using least privilege identity?
SEC1.notes:
Evidence: USER app (uid/gid 10001, no login shell) in both Dockerfiles; read-only root filesystem.
Gap: None significant.

SEC2.title: How do you control access to your build infrastructure?
SEC2.notes:
Evidence: CodeBuild and CodePipeline roles are scoped to their repositories, buckets, log group and services; no long-lived credentials in the pipeline.
Gap: The only human identity has AdministratorAccess without MFA, so administrator access to the build infrastructure is not limited.

SEC3.title: How do you detect and address vulnerabilities within your container image?
SEC3.notes:
Evidence: ECR scan on push for every image; findings reviewed and the decision documented (Phase 2).
Gap: Basic (OS-only) scanning; no Inspector enhanced scanning; no gate that blocks images with critical findings.

SEC4.title: How do you manage your container image boundaries?
SEC4.notes:
Evidence: Minimal attack surface: slim base, no compilers, pip removed, non-root user, read-only filesystem, only port 3000 exposed, no shell access/ECS Exec.
Gap: Lineage is not recorded: provenance/SBOM attestations were disabled to keep a single manifest; no image signing.

SEC5.title: How do you handle data within your containerized applications?
SEC5.notes:
Evidence: No secrets in images or the repo (Secrets Manager valueFrom, secret scans before commits); persistent data outside the containers (Aurora, DynamoDB).
Gap: None significant.
